fixed.explanation: With only header rows, the parser returns empty columns whose number of levels differs from header_names. The unconditional set_names call then raises a ValueError. I guard the call so that names are applied only when the level count matches. This lets the empty DataFrame be returned, as read_csv does. I did not see the parser code that builds those columns, so this is a best guess.

query.intent: Excel reader's parsing of header rows with multiple header lines and index_col (TextParser/_parse_sheet in read_excel) fails when the data has only header rows and no data rows; it should return an empty DataFrame with a MultiIndex columns like read_csv does.
query.symptom: read_excel with header=[0,1] and index_col=0 raises an error on a sheet with only header rows, whereas read_csv returns an empty DataFrame.

history.analysis: _parse_sheet builds header_names and has_index_names before TextParser runs. The error with header-only data may come from PythonParser, which handles multi-row headers with index_col and empty data, rather than from this function. I need to see that code.
